main_text.l: Conscientia. Atqui ego adulterium & homicidium perpetraui.
Synterefis. Frugi adolescenti in timore Dei, summo studio in bonis literis versandum, nec frustranda spes paretum & propinquorum, nec fides magistratui data fallenda est.
Conscientia. Tu vero nec pietatem erga Deum, nec diligentiam in studijs, nec reuerentiam praeceptoribus debitam, nec alias virtutes studioso homine dignas, unquam praestare & probare stu-duisti.
Quare non dubium est, te iratu habere Deum, & maledictu esse, ac poenas aeternas daturum, nisi resipiscas.

8. Finis est, ut fit conscientia illustre testimonium de iudicio Dei, quod tum maxime lucet, cum male sibi conscios in mediis successibus, [illegible, ~14 letters] & anxios reddit:bene autem sibi conscios, in morte ipsa exhilarat & reficit. Prodest autem ex historijs petere exempla euentuum, qui fuerunt testimonia de syllogismis [?]istis. Cain, Ahitophel, Iudas Iscariotes, Saul

page.notes: The Greek word after "successibus" is too faint to read reliably, so it is marked illegible. The word "istis" in the last line of the text is doubtful, as is the Greek on the line "4.". The word "Saul" is set indented at the end of the paragraph and is counted as text, not as a catchword. The word "iratu" is printed as is.
